title: Secure Cloud Operator: Verification and Visibility
objectives: Verify IAM user identity using sts get-caller-identity
List S3 buckets with s3 ls command
Describe EC2 instances with ec2 describe-instances

mission_brief.situation: As a cloud operator, you need to ensure the security of your AWS resources.
mission_brief.mission: Verify the identity of IAM users and inspect S3 buckets and EC2 instances for potential issues.
mission_brief.execution: Use the correct AWS CLI commands to gather information without creating any resources.

prerequisites: AWS credentials configured on local machine

content.concept:
Verification and visibility are crucial for securing cloud resources. This lesson focuses on using the right AWS CLI commands to inspect and verify your environment without creating new resources.

This section reinforces secure, repeatable, audit-safe cloud operations using deterministic, read-only validation techniques suitable for any sandbox or production-like environment.
content.walkthrough: In this walkthrough, we will go over three essential AWS CLI commands: sts get-caller-identity for IAM user verification, s3 ls for listing S3 buckets, and ec2 describe-instances for EC2 instance details. Each command is carefully chosen to provide the required information without modifying your environment.
checkpoints: List all S3 buckets in your account
common_mistakes: Using creation commands instead of inspection commands
Ignoring critical security issues in the environment

lab.setup: Ensure you have AWS CLI installed and configured on your local machine.
safety: Be cautious when listing S3 buckets as this may show sensitive data.
Avoid modifying any resources or permissions during this exercise.
Keep your AWS credentials secure at all times.

elite_competence.role_simulation: You are the cloud security lead and have been alerted to a potential threat. Your task is to quickly verify IAM user permissions, inspect S3 buckets for unusual activity, and check EC2 instances for any signs of compromise.

bug_injection.bug: A rogue IAM user has gained elevated privileges
bug_injection.symptom: Unexpected changes in S3 bucket access patterns
bug_injection.fix: Revoke the IAM user's permissions and rotate credentials

pass_conditions: Correctly identify the rogue IAM user
List all S3 buckets with unusual activity
Describe EC2 instances with signs of compromise
fail_conditions: Incorrectly identified IAM user or permissions issue
Failed to list S3 buckets due to lack of credentials

interrogation_questions: What are the first steps in responding to a security threat?
How would you investigate unusual activity in S3 buckets?
What measures can be taken to prevent future security breaches?

legal_context.allowed: Using AWS CLI commands for verification and inspection purposes
legal_context.prohibited: Creating new resources or modifying existing ones without explicit permission

resume_bullets: Verified IAM user identity using sts get-caller-identity command
Listed all S3 buckets with s3 ls command
Described active EC2 instances with ec2 describe-instances command
